turns.prompt_text: is there a program, AI, or software that can generate Figma layouts?
turns.response_html:
Yes, there are several powerful programs and AI tools specifically designed to generate and iterate on Figma layouts. As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from simple "text-to-image" to tools that generate fully editable layers and components.

Here are the top options based on your needs:

1. Figma's Native AI (Figma Make / First Draft)

Figma recently launched its own native AI suite, accessible directly via the action button (⌘ + K or Ctrl + K).

  • What it does: You can type a prompt like "e-commerce dashboard for a plant shop," and it will generate multi-screen layouts using actual Figma frames and auto-layout.
  • Best feature: It can be trained to use your own design system and components, so the layouts it generates aren't just generic—they match your brand’s specific buttons, colors, and typography.

2. Galileo AI

Widely considered the "ChatGPT for UI," Galileo is a standalone tool that specializes in high-fidelity interface generation.

  • What it does: It generates complex, professional UI screens from natural language prompts.
  • Figma Integration: Once you generate a design in Galileo, you can copy it directly into Figma as editable vector layers. It is particularly good at mobile app flows and landing pages.

3. UX Pilot

This is a powerful Figma plugin focused on the early stages of the design process.

  • What it does: It generates wireframes, high-fidelity screens, and even full user flows (sitemaps) directly inside your project.
  • Unique edge: It includes AI-powered design reviews and predictive heatmaps to show where users might look on your generated layout before you even test it.

4. Uizard (Autodesigner)

Uizard is a separate design platform, but it is highly compatible with Figma workflows.

  • What it does: Its "Autodesigner" creates full UI mockups from text.
  • The "Magic" Feature: You can take a photo of a hand-drawn sketch on a napkin or a screenshot of an existing app, and Uizard will convert it into an editable digital layout that you can then export to Figma.

5. Builder.io (Visual Copilot)

If you are moving from design to development, this is a top-tier choice.

  • What it does: It can take a text prompt and generate a layout, but its real power is in Code to Canvas. It can take existing code (like a React component) and turn it back into a Figma layout, or vice versa.

turns.prompt_text: What are some good UI/UX AIs
turns.response_html:
In early 2026, the term "UI/UX AI" has evolved from simple image generators into specialized "agents" that handle different parts of the design lifecycle—from user research to production-ready code.

Since you're exploring generative software, here are the top AI tools categorized by their specific "superpowers":

1. The "Vibe-to-Code" Leaders

These tools are the biggest trend of 2026, allowing you to design by describing the "vibe" and getting a functional app in return.

  • Emergent: A full-stack AI platform that doesn't just design screens; it builds the backend and frontend simultaneously. It’s perfect if you want a UI that actually works with real data right away.
  • Lovable: Famous for "vibe coding." You chat with it to build full-stack applications. It’s excellent for rapid prototyping where you need to move beyond a clickable mockup into a real, hosted app.

2. Professional UI Generators

These tools focus on high-fidelity visual design and design system consistency.

  • Galileo AI: Still the industry gold standard for turning text into editable Figma designs. It has a high "design sense" and creates layouts that look like they were made by a senior designer.
  • Banani: A newer, high-speed generator that focuses on branding. You can upload your brand guidelines, and it ensures every generated screen follows your specific aesthetic, spacing, and colors.
  • Google Stitch: Deeply integrated with Material Design. If you are building for Android or ChromeOS, this is the most "correct" tool for ensuring your UI follows platform standards.

3. UX Research & Strategy AIs

UX is more than just how it looks; these tools help with the "thinking" part of design.

  • QoQo (Figma Plugin): An essential for the discovery phase. It generates user personas, journey maps, and interview scripts based on your product brief.
  • Synthetic Users: A unique (and somewhat controversial) tool that lets you run usability tests on "AI participants" modeled after your target audience. It’s great for "pre-testing" an idea before spending a budget on human testers.
  • UX Pilot: The best "all-rounder" for UX. It handles wireframing, generates user flows, and even provides AI-powered heatmaps to predict where users will click.

4. Website-Specific Builders

  • Framer AI: The best for marketing sites. It generates a layout and then lets you publish it as a live website with high-end animations in one click.
  • Relume: Focuses on the "skeleton." It uses AI to build sitemaps and wireframes using a library of thousands of pre-built components.

Comparison at a Glance
